title: Manager prep + self-review notes Q4 2025
content:
Purpose: prep notes for upcoming skip-level + manager 1:1 and quarterly self-review. Keep this loose - bullets I want to actually say and a few data points to back them up.

Quick wins / accomplishments (since Jul 2025):
- Reduced average time-to-hire for SWE role funnel from ~42 -> 29 days (small sample: two pods). Key levers: interview guide consolidation, clearer score rubric, and faster offer turnarounds.
- Launched Manager Onboarding module (pilot) - 64% completion rate in first cohort, NPS ~6.8/10 (survey sample n=25). Early feedback: module is practical but wants more examples for mid-level IC->manager transition.
- Rolled out standardized interview training to 45 hiring managers; self-reported confidence up by ~20% in post-training survey.
- Negotiated benefits vendor renewal - moved to tiered pricing, expected 12% cost savings YOY for 2026 plan.
- Built out basic hiring dashboard (with infra/data team) that surfaces pipeline by stage and lead time; used weekly by Recruiting and Eng leads.

Impact highlights (concrete):
- Faster hiring correlates with 10% lower lost-offer rate for top candidates in pilot teams.
- Manager onboarding pilot shortened ramp to first direct report 1:1 cadence (baseline moved from 6 -> 4 weeks in pilot).

Areas I want to own / strategic focus (next 6 months):
1) Manager enablement program v1.0 - expand onboarding pilot into a repeatable program with blended learning + coaching. Goal: 80% completion and +1pt NPS improvement.
2) Calibration and performance process improvements - create a lightweight rubric + training for managers to improve fairness and speed.
3) Hiring velocity + quality: expand interview guide changes org-wide, run A/B on structured vs unstructured scorecards.
4) Career framework gap analysis - partner with compensation to define clearer ladder for Sr IC/Staff levels.

Concrete asks for my manager in the 1:1 / skip-level:
- Approval to hire: +1 Recruiting Operations head (contractor -> FTE) for H1 2026. Rationale: capacity to scale hiring programs + data ops.
- Budget sign-off for manager coaching pilot ($18k for 6 months external coach + platform).
- Support in getting 2 Eng directors aligned for calibration pilot (need their buy-in to run in Jan).
- Feedback: areas I should prioritize that will have highest leverage for org health (want prioritized list).

Risks / blockers:
- Data reliability: hiring dashboard still has gaps for contract hires and international locations - need a small data sprint.
- Manager time: many managers are overloaded, low capacity to complete training modules unless we make them <30min or justify as mission-critical.
- Headcount constraints: if we can't convert the contractor raise, timeline for hiring programs slips by ~2 quarters.

Self-review notes (framing for conversation):
- Strengths: operational follow-through (ship programs), cross-functional partnership (Product/Eng/Recruiting), data-driven decisions.
- Development areas: strategic influence at exec level (need to move from tactical wins to org-wide strategies), delegating deeper - too much hands-on in initial implementation.
- Example of leadership: led interview guide changes - coordinated with 5 hiring committees, created training + rolled out in 6 weeks. Outcome: measurable reduction in time-to-hire in pilot teams.
- Example of where I need help: getting exec-level prioritization for manager enablement - need manager to escalate and model participation.

Feedback I want to solicit (specific):
- Am I focusing on the right OKRs for People Ops this year? (Hiring velocity, manager enablement, calibration)
- Is the proposed +1 recruiter ops hire justified vs re-prioritizing existing headcount?
- How visible should I make the manager enablement program to the leadership team now? (soft launch vs announce)

Notes to self - how to say it in the meeting:
- Start with two quick wins (hiring metric + onboarding pilot NPS) to set positive tone.
- Pivot to strategic ask: we need one recruiter ops head to scale the tooling and data; detail ROI (reduced time-to-hire, fewer contractor costs).
- Give precise ask: sign-off for budget ($18k) and permission to run pilot with 2 Eng directors in Jan.
- Close with a request for 1-2 introductions (CTO/Product leads) and an explicit follow-up: "I'll send a 1-pager + proposed timeline, can you share with X and Y?"

Open questions / TODOs (personal checklist):
- Draft 1-pager for headcount + budget ask - due 2026-02-25.
- Finalize Eng director list for calibration pilot - action: Priya to confirm by 2026-02-15.
- Quick data cleanup task: join sync with DataOps to add contractor types to dashboard - scheduled 2026-02-22.
- Collect manager quotes for program landing page (3 short blurbs) - target 2026-03-01.

Raw snippets / example phrasing I might use:
- "Pilot showed a ~30% reduction in time-to-hire in two pods; with modest investment we can scale and capture that across core product teams."
- "This is about manager bandwidth: coaching + simple tooling reduces escalations and improves retention - small spend, outsized effect."

Linked docs I may reference in the meeting:
- Hiring dashboard (link above)
- Manager onboarding pilot deck (Confluence) - page: HR-OKRs-2025 -> Manager Onboarding Pilot
- Interview guide v2 (Google doc linked in Slack thread #hiring-tools)

Random personal notes (keep short):
- Remember to ask about support for speaking at the all-hands on manager enablement (public visibility helps).
- Bring up career framework urgency - several ICs asked for clarity; wins there will reduce attrition risk.

End of file - will iterate after prep call with Priya.
